data.author: Sana, from Iran
data.story: When I first arrived in Perugia, I felt a bit lost. The language was a barrier, and the bureaucracy seemed overwhelming. However, I used the resources from the university and connected with other international students. I focused on my studies, and after two years, I graduated with top marks. My advice is to be patient, ask for help, and never give up on your goals. Now, I work as a software engineer in Milan!

data.author: David, from the USA
data.story: I came to Perugia to immerse myself in the Italian language. The city is the perfect size – big enough to be interesting, but small enough to feel like home. I joined a local tandem language exchange group and made many Italian friends. The key was to practice speaking every single day, even when it was difficult. After a year, I was fluent and had a deep appreciation for the culture.

data.author: Fatima, from Morocco
data.story: The path to studying medicine in Italy is long, but it's worth it. The university has excellent professors. I struggled with some of the exams, but I formed a study group with my classmates, and we supported each other. The ADiSU scholarship was also a huge help financially. My success came from discipline and teamwork.
